Package org.aeonbits.owner.extras.validation

package org.aeonbits.owner.extras.validation
The Bean Validation provider the core looks for: what makes @Min, @NotNull and the rest mean something on a method named the way this library teaches.

They did not, and quietly. Validator.validate(object) walks JavaBean properties, so @Min(12) int getPort() was checked and @Min(12) int port() was not - an annotation that reads like a guarantee and is not one. BeanValidator checks the value each method resolves to, and ViolationPath reports it under the key the property is read with rather than under the name of a getter nobody wrote.

Both spellings of the specification are supported and neither is required: JakartaBeanValidation and JavaxBeanValidation are the only classes that name jakarta.validation and javax.validation, so that the validator itself can be discovered and instantiated on a class path that has neither.
